target.title: fix(slack): time out stalled external file uploads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack's external file-upload flow could wait forever after media had been loaded into memory if the presigned byte-upload endpoint accepted the connection but never returned a response. The outbound delivery queue then remained blocked, and treating the timeout like an ordinary ambiguous send would also strand the queued file even though Slack had not finalized it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The production byte `POST` now has a 120-second budget. The timer ends before `files.completeUploadExternal`: Slack's completion call is commit-capable and one-shot, so timing it out or broadly retrying it would create unknown-send and duplicate-file semantics.

The channel adapter reports a typed not-dispatched outcome only when the byte transfer times out before completion dispatch. Durable delivery clears send-attempt evidence and permits replay only when every failure branch proves that boundary; mixed aggregates, forged codes, prior sends, and completion failures remain conservative.

Transport policy keeps the shipped alternate-API-root contract: standard Slack and GovSlack accept only their exact HTTPS upload hosts, while an explicitly configured Slack-compatible API root may return an upload URL on that exact origin. Capability-bearing paths and queries are excluded from routine logs and guarded-fetch capture.

## User Impact

Stalled Slack file uploads now fail after a bounded interval and can be retried safely instead of holding media memory and the delivery queue indefinitely. Successful uploads and long-running completion calls keep their existing one-shot behavior. Thanks @zhangguiping-xydt for the original report and fix.

## Evidence

- Exact head `b5f3b2f03ce87578d09d086976d4e66c87b7290a`, sanitized Linux x64 Crabbox `run_7eca84346708`: 306 focused Slack/queue/SDK tests passed, the plugin SDK API baseline passed, and `check:changed` passed.
- Live controlled Slack upload boundary, Crabbox `run_d45327b481b6`: a real 104-byte PNG followed production media loading, the production SSRF guard, managed proxy, CONNECT, TLS, and raw byte transport. The success control dispatched and completed once; the hanging POST failed at 120.035s as `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError` with a `TimeoutError` cause and zero dispatch/completion; an original completion remained pending for 123.064s and then succeeded without timeout or retry. The hanging connection closed, all received bytes matched, and the capability path/query was absent from output.
- Source-blind behavior validation passed every in-scope contract clause with no findings.
- Fresh autoreview: full branch clean at confidence 0.86; final Linux runtime-fetch harness correction clean at confidence 0.98.
- Authenticated Slack URL negotiation and workspace routing were substituted by a controlled Slack control plane because the sanitized runner has no workspace credentials. The transport and delivery-state paths under test are production paths.

target.title: Refresh MCP OAuth auth-profile tokens
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Remote MCP servers such as Ducktape can be configured with static `Authorization` headers today. That makes an otherwise refresh-capable OAuth credential decay into dead bearer text, so tool discovery/calls fail once the access token expires.

This PR lets OpenClaw own that refresh path for remote MCP servers by binding a server to an existing refresh-capable auth profile:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "ducktape": {
        "url": "https://agents.ducktape.xyz/mcp",
        "transport": "streamable-http",
        "auth": "oauth",
        "oauth": {
          "authProfileId": "ducktape:mcp"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Why This Change Was Made

James linked the Ducktape MCP expired-token failure and asked OpenClaw to own token refresh instead of relying on a James-specific cron or static config rewrite.

This keeps existing MCP-native OAuth behavior unchanged: `auth: "oauth"` without `oauth.authProfileId` still uses MCP SDK OAuth login and `openclaw mcp login`. Setting `oauth.authProfileId` is an explicit auth selector for refresh-capable OpenClaw OAuth profiles.

## Summary

- Added `mcp.servers.*.oauth.authProfileId` to config schema/types/help/labels/docs.
- Added an MCP auth-profile resolver that loads the selected auth profile, requires a refreshable OAuth credential, reuses existing `resolveApiKeyForProfile` refresh/locking/store behavior, strips stale static `Authorization` headers, and never projects refresh tokens downstream.
- MCP bearer projection now uses the resolved raw OAuth credential access token, not provider-formatted `apiKey` output. This prevents Google-style structured auth payloads from becoming `Authorization: Bearer {"token":...}`.
- Wired auth-profile bearer injection into embedded/session MCP HTTP transports, CLI bundle MCP projection via per-server token env vars, and local native Codex app-server user MCP projection.
- Kept Codex app-server bearer projection local-only: remote app-server connections fail closed before resolving/projecting auth-profile bearers.
- Redacted literal app-server Authorization headers before computing the user-MCP resume fingerprint, while retaining a one-way `sha256` lifecycle marker so bearer changes rebuild the Codex app-server MCP binding.
- Preserved exact OpenClaw `toolFilter.include` / `toolFilter.exclude` projection into Codex `enabled_tools` / `disabled_tools`; wildcard filters fail closed because Codex only supports exact tool-name sets here.
- Merged current `origin/main` into the PR branch in `89ac88be72` and resolved conflicts in `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` and `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts`.

## User Impact

Operators can keep remote MCP servers bound to refreshable OAuth profiles instead of copying expiring bearer tokens into config. Existing `auth: "oauth"` MCP-native login setups keep their current behavior unless they opt into `oauth.authProfileId`.

For local Codex app-server threads, OpenClaw intentionally materializes the current access token as a native MCP `Authorization` header because Codex receives MCP client config. This is not enabled for remote app-server connections; maintainers still need to own that local trust-boundary decision before merge.

## Evidence

Focused post-merge tests:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts src/agents/mcp-auth-profile.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-codex.user-config.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.user-mcp-servers.test.ts test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts
```

Result: passed 4 Vitest shards / 136 tests.

Focused token-shape rerun after `225b4be6db`:

```text
corepack pnpm vitest run src/agents/mcp-auth-profile.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-codex.user-config.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.user-mcp-servers.test.ts
```

Result: passed 7 Vitest project files / 132 tests.

Tooling rerun after lint cleanup:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts
```

Result: passed 1 Vitest shard / 8 tests.

SDK surface compatibility:

```text

node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-subpath-exports.mjs
node scripts/sync-plugin-sdk-exports.mjs --check
```

Result: passed. Public package SDK budgets are now `323` entrypoints / `10413` exports / `5228` callable exports after retaining the shipped `openclaw/plugin-sdk/codex-mcp-projection` subpath and merging current `main`.

Lint / whitespace:

```text
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/mcp-auth-profile.ts src/agents/mcp-auth-profile.test.ts src/agents/mcp-transport.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-types.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts src/agents/codex-mcp-config.ts src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp.ts src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-codex.ts src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-codex.user-config.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/codex-mcp-projection.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.user-mcp-servers.test.ts src/config/types.mcp.ts src/config/zod-schema.ts src/config/schema.test.ts src/config/schema.labels.ts src/config/schema.help.ts scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts
```

Result: passed.

```text

```

Result: passed.

Type gate rerun after `225b4be6db`:

```text
corepack pnpm tsgo:test:src
```

Result: passed locally.

## Real Behavior Proof

- Behavior addressed: auth-profile-backed MCP servers no longer project stale static Authorization headers; OpenClaw resolves the refresh-capable OAuth profile and passes only the current bearer token downstream.
- Real environment tested: local macOS checkout on the PR branch, Node 24, temp OpenClaw auth-profile SQLite store, temp localhost HTTP MCP proof server.
- Proof command used earlier in this PR: `node --import tsx --input-type=module` proof script importing `resolveMcpAuthProfileBundleConfig` and `withMcpAuthProfileBearer`, writing a temp OAuth auth profile, starting a localhost MCP proof server, projecting the MCP config, and calling the server through both projected CLI config and same-origin wrapped fetch paths.
- Observed proof result: downstream MCP client config had no OpenClaw-only `auth`/`oauth` fields, no refresh token, no stale Authorization value, and the local proof server exposed `proof.echo` only when it received the current OAuth-profile bearer.

What was not tested: this proof uses a local refresh-capable OAuth profile and local MCP server, not live Ducktape credentials. No real third-party tokens are included. Live Ducktape remains an explicit maintainer/operator acceptance item.

## Remaining Limitations

- This PR adds the generic OpenClaw-owned refresh/projection path, but it does not mutate any live operator config such as Hedwig's current Ducktape server entry.
- Live Ducktape proof still requires a real `ducktape:mcp` style OAuth auth profile binding in config. No real credentials are included in this branch or PR.
